definitions.explanation: To expose something to air or sun to remove moisture.

examples.japanese: {洗濯物|せんたくもの}を{干|ほ}す。
examples.english: I hang the laundry out to dry.

examples.japanese: {布団|ふとん}を{干|ほ}して{日光|にっこう}{消毒|しょうどく}する。
examples.english: I air out the futon to disinfect it with sunlight.

notes:
{干|ほ}す means to dry something by exposing it to air or sun.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {乾|かわ}く (intransitive, to dry)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {洗濯物|せんたくもの}を{干|ほ}す: to hang laundry to dry
- {布団|ふとん}を{干|ほ}す: to air out a futon
- {干|ほ}し{物|もの}: things hung out to dry
- {干|ほ}し{竿|ざお}: drying pole

RELATED WORDS:
- {干物|ひもの}: dried fish
- {干|ほ}しぶどう: raisins (dried grapes)
- {梅干|うめぼ}し: pickled plum

The kanji {干|ほ}す relates to drying/draining.
